basis: The task's inputs come from OCHA's Financial Tracking Service through two instruments. (1) The publisher's own use-and-republish page ('About FTS / Using FTS data', read 2026-10-29, quoted in the candidate record's license_evidence): FTS encourages fair use of its data and explicitly permits copying and re-using data published on the FTS website/API, contemplating amended and derived data, with a citation request naming FTS, the publication date of the figures and the relevant URL, and for amended/combined data a citation of the form '[YOU/YOUR ORGANIZATION]... based on Financial Tracking Service (FTS) data, [DATE], [URL]'. (2) The HDX bulk distribution of the identical requirements-and-funding data (fts_requirements_funding_global.csv, the vintage cross-check input) carries CC BY-IGO on its HDX dataset record (read 2026-10-29), permitting reproduction, distribution and derivative works with attribution and the no-endorsement condition. The plan/flow records used to build the panel come from the public anonymous HPC/FTS API, which the FTS reuse terms cover. Class A: explicit permission for redistribution and derivatives with attribution. Standing defaults apply: our code and documentation are MIT, our rights in the derived compilation are dedicated CC0-1.0, and the source's own terms are preserved, never relicensed.

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the single-country-appeal eligibility frame (one-country CSV groups with a positive launch-vintage original requirements figure, plan years 2000-2025), the counted exclusions (multi-country regional groups, no-orig groups, the pre-window and the 2026+ live edge as unobserved-target censoring), the derived binary label (year-end funding >= 50% of original launch-vintage requirements), the appeal-recency feature computed only from the YEARS of strictly-earlier same-country appeals, the launch-instant temporal partition, and the packaging - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying FTS/HPC data keeps its own terms and attribution requirements, which carry through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

conditions: The FTS attribution request is carried in every copy of the data and its documentation, in FTS's own suggested form for derived data.
The CC BY-IGO attribution and no-endorsement conditions on the HDX bulk input carry through unchanged to the derived data.
The dataset is labelled as derived and never presented as an OCHA or FTS official product.

Changes are indicated: the dataset ships a row selection (single-country appeals with positive launch asks, plan years 2000-2025), counted exclusions (multi-country groups, no-orig groups, live-edge unobserved targets), a derived binary label (>= 50% of launch-vintage original requirements covered by year end), an appeal-recency feature reading only prior appeal YEARS, and a launch-instant temporal partition.
Our contribution is dedicated CC0-1.0; the source's own terms are preserved and carry through unchanged, and CC0 is never presented as the source's licence.
Our code and documentation are MIT.

operator_acceptance.note: No operator acceptance is needed or recorded: the source's own instruments (the FTS use-and-republish terms and CC BY-IGO on the HDX record) explicitly permit redistribution and derivatives with attribution, and this release stays within them.
